sections.h2: Where is Lexington County and what does it include?
sections.html:
Lexington County is in the Midlands of South Carolina and is part of the Columbia metropolitan area. It covers 757.62 square miles, with 58.62 of those square miles being water, mostly because of Lake Murray.

The town of Lexington is the county seat and largest community, with 23,568 residents in 2020. West Columbia, Cayce, Irmo, Batesburg-Leesville, Chapin and Gaston are among the other municipalities, and large unincorporated places include Seven Oaks, Oak Grove, Red Bank and White Knoll. Parts of Columbia, Cayce, Irmo and Batesburg-Leesville cross county lines into Richland or Saluda counties.

Neighbors are Richland, Orangeburg, Calhoun, Aiken, Saluda and Newberry counties. Development has concentrated in the eastern and northeastern parts, which is the side nearest Columbia. A lake-area house, a subdivision near Irmo and a rural parcel near Gilbert are all in one county, but they sell on very different timelines.

sections.h2: How fast has Lexington County grown?
sections.html:
Lexington County grew from 262,391 residents in 2010 to 293,991 in the 2020 census, an increase of 12.0 percent. Its estimate for 2025 is 317,588, which makes it the sixth most populous county in the state.

The county was chartered in 1785 and named for Lexington, Massachusetts. About 74.8 percent of residents lived in urban areas in 2020. Rapid growth tends to raise assessed values at the next reassessment, so a seller who bought several years ago may see a bigger tax bill than the one they planned around.

sections.h2: What drives the Lexington County economy?
sections.html:
Health care, retail and food service lead Lexington County employment, and the county's 2022 gross domestic product was $16.7 billion. In the third quarter of 2023 health care and social assistance supplied 14.9 percent of jobs, retail 13.9 percent and accommodation and food services 9.9 percent.

The employers listed for 2021 were:

  • Lexington Medical Center, 7,893 employees
  • Lexington School District 1, 3,674
  • Amazon, 3,050
  • Walmart, 2,603
  • State government, 2,308
  • Michelin, 2,240
  • County of Lexington, 1,855

Distribution centers cluster in the Saxe Gotha Industrial Park near Cayce. The mix of hospitals, schools and state jobs gives the county steadier housing demand than a single-industry county, though it does not protect an individual house with a leaking roof from sitting unsold.

sections.h2: What roads, schools and weather should a Lexington County seller know about?
sections.html:
Three interstates touch Lexington County: I-20, I-26 and I-77, which begins in Cayce. Columbia Metropolitan Airport serves the area and the COMET authority provides public transit.

Five school districts cover parts of the county, and District 1 is the largest, with 27,072 students and 31 schools. Midlands Technical College and the county library system are also based here.

The climate is humid. Average rainfall is about 47 inches a year, with a July high near 92 degrees and a January low near 33 degrees. Wet summers are hard on roofs, gutters and crawl spaces, and a house on or near Lake Murray or the Saluda, Broad and Congaree rivers should be checked for drainage and flood questions before a buyer's inspector does it.

sections.h2: Who do you contact about Lexington County property tax?
sections.html:
The Treasurer collects, the Assessor values the property and the Auditor handles exemptions. All three are county offices with their own numbers:

  • Treasurer: 212 South Lake Drive, Suite 101, Lexington, SC 29072; (803) 785-8217; open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
  • Delinquent Tax Department: (803) 785-8345
  • Tax Assessor: (803) 785-8190, for exemptions, sales, address changes, appraisals and rollback taxes
  • Auditor: (803) 785-8181, for homestead exemptions and refunds

Payments can be made in person, online at lex-co.sc.gov, by mailed check to PO Box 604397, Charlotte, NC 28260-4397, or through the night deposit box in front of the County Administration Building. Card payments carry convenience fees, and the postmark decides whether a mailed check is late.

sections.h2: When are Lexington County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Lexington County real property notices are mailed to the owner of record after October 1, and full payment is due by January 15 of the next year. Payments postmarked after that date pick up penalties on January 16, February 2 and March 17.

The Treasurer's page does not give the percentages, but S.C. Code 12-45-180 sets them at 3 percent, then an added 7 percent, then an added 5 percent. Penalties keep accruing during a penalty appeal unless the full amount is paid, and the county refunds penalties already paid if the appeal is granted. The Treasurer takes written penalty appeals; call (803) 785-8217 for instructions.

The county also runs an installment program for real property that is not paid through escrow. Enrollees make five advance payments based on the prior year's tax, and the balance is billed by November 15. Enrollment renews each year until the owner opts out in writing, which matters if you sell: tell the Treasurer so a renewal does not bill the next owner's account.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Lexington County assessment?
sections.html:
A Lexington County owner files a written appeal with the Assessor within 90 days of the date on the assessment notice. If no notice arrived, the county's FAQ says the window is January 1 through January 15 of the following year.

The county reviews appeals on market value, and disagreeing with the dollar amount of the bill is not a ground. If the appeal is not resolved by December 31, the bill is based on at least 80 percent of the assessed value, and tax is still due January 15. After resolution, you either get a refund with interest or owe the difference with interest.

The county has a nine-member Board of Assessment Appeals appointed by County Council. It meets when requested in the Council Chambers of the County Administration Building, and its agendas are posted on the county meeting portal. The state notice rule applies as well: notices are required when value rises $1,000 or more, and the county page says the previous reassessments were in 2015 and 2020 on a five-year cycle, so ask the Assessor for the current schedule.

sections.h2: What changes when a Lexington County house is sold?
sections.html:
The seller's unpaid tax is settled from the proceeds at closing, and the buyer must apply for the 4 percent legal residence ratio. State law says that application must be filed before the first penalty date of the year the owner first claims it.

Common seller problems in Lexington County include:

  • A rental house that fails the 72-day limit and carries the 6 percent ratio.
  • Installment enrollment that nobody canceled after a sale.
  • A bill sent to an old address because the Assessor was never told about a move.
  • A lake or older neighborhood house needing a roof, septic or foundation work before a lender will approve a buyer.

If the tax is behind and repairs are the obstacle, an as-is cash sale lets the title company pay the county out of proceeds. The Delinquent Tax Department at (803) 785-8345 can give you the payoff, and the Treasurer's page does not describe tax sale dates, so ask that office directly.

faqs.q: What is the Lexington County property tax due date?
faqs.a: Full payment is due by January 15 of the year after the tax year, per the county Treasurer. Penalties begin on January 16.

faqs.q: Where is the Lexington County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: It is at 212 South Lake Drive, Suite 101, Lexington, SC 29072. The phone is (803) 785-8217 and hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Lexington County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 90 days from the date on the assessment notice. If you never received one, the county says to appeal between January 1 and January 15 of the following year.

faqs.q: Does Lexington County have an installment plan?
faqs.a: Yes, for real property not paid through escrow. You make five advance payments based on last year's tax, and the balance is billed by November 15.

faqs.q: Can I mail my Lexington County tax payment?
faqs.a: Yes, by check only, to PO Box 604397, Charlotte, NC 28260-4397. The U.S. postmark decides whether it is late.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lexington County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the balance from the sale proceeds at closing. Call the Delinquent Tax Department at (803) 785-8345 for the current amount.
